finding: This revision replaced item 5's catch-all with a two-test enumeration and thereby orphaned a third test, while item 4 positively asserts the opposite. Round 3's item 5 read "The remaining `sel.Maintainability` and `MaintainabilityFileCap` references in `internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go` are renamed mechanically" — a sweep that covered every remaining reference in the file. Round 4 narrows it to "`TestFilterFiles_Maintainability` and `TestFilterFiles_DropFirstBackfill`". But `TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted` — item 4's own test — also references the renamed field twice, at internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go:123 (`require.Len(t, sel.Maintainability, 1)`) and :124 (`assert.Equal(t, "keep.go", sel.Maintainability[0].Path)`). §2.5 renames that field to `CodeFiles`, so those two lines do not compile after the rename, yet item 4 states "That one line references a removed field and is deleted, not renamed; the rest of the test stands." The rest of the test does not stand. An implementer following §2.8 literally deletes line 125, leaves 123-124, and ships a package that fails `go build ./...` — in the one section whose entire value is its claim to be an exhaustive inventory, and produced by the very edit that was meant to make item 5 checkable by name.

resolved.evidence: Confirmed by the new mechanical check: TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted references both sel.Security and sel.Maintainability. §2.8 item 4 now states both changes — the sel.Security line is deleted, the two sel.Maintainability lines are renamed to CodeFiles — so item 4 and item 5 no longer contradict each other and no reference is orphaned by the narrowing.

suggestion: Either restore item 5's file-wide sweep alongside the two named tests ("…and every remaining `sel.Maintainability` / `MaintainabilityFileCap` reference in the file, including the two in `TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted`"), or amend item 4 to state both edits: the `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)` line is deleted, and the two surviving `sel.Maintainability` references at :123-124 are renamed to `sel.CodeFiles` — replacing "the rest of the test stands".

finding: §2.8 claims exhaustiveness against a search for `sel.Maintainability`, but its per-item dispositions contradict the search result for one test. Item 4 says of `TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted` that only the `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)` line goes and 'the rest of the test stands' — yet that test also holds `require.Len(t, sel.Maintainability, 1)` and `assert.Equal(t, "keep.go", sel.Maintainability[0].Path)` (internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go:123-124), which do not compile after §2.5 renames the field to `CodeFiles`. Item 5, which is written as the enumeration of the `sel.Maintainability`/`MaintainabilityFileCap` tests that get the mechanical rename, names only `TestFilterFiles_Maintainability` and `TestFilterFiles_DropFirstBackfill`. An implementer following item 4 literally leaves the package non-compiling, and the section that is declared to be 'the contract' is wrong about one of its own eight entries.

resolved.evidence: Same contradiction as the regression lens's incomplete-rename-inventory finding, fixed together in §2.8 item 4. The disposition now matches what the search actually returns, and scripts/check-test-inventory.py enforces that agreement mechanically from here on.

suggestion: Amend item 4 to read: delete the `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)` line and rename this test's two `sel.Maintainability` references to `sel.CodeFiles`; the rest stands. Or add `TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted` to item 5's rename list and have item 4 cover only the deleted line.

finding: §4 mandates that README.md, skills/tp/SKILL.md, skills/tp/REFERENCE.md and CLAUDE.md each contain the literal substring `spec-coverage is the only reserved auditor id`, and §7 item 14 locks that substring in with a guard test. That claim contradicts an existing role-corpus invariant this spec never says it changes: the one shared role parser reserves the id `regression` for reviewer AND auditor files — REFERENCE.md line 367 states `id` (MUST equal the filename stem, `^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$`, not the reserved `regression`), README.md line 579 and SKILL.md line 222 repeat it, and CLAUDE.md's role-corpus rule says `regression` reserved. After this release REFERENCE.md would assert, two sections apart, both that `regression` is a reserved role id and that `spec-coverage` is the ONLY reserved auditor id, and a user following the new sentence would author .tp/auditors/regression.json and hit the exit-3 malformed-role abort. §4's own requirement is that the four documents 'must all tell one story'; the mandated sentence breaks that story, and §2.1's `roleSpecCoverage` remains as the one reserved id inherits the same collision.

resolved.evidence: Real collision, verified: REFERENCE.md's Role Corpus schema already reserves `regression` as an id in both phases, so 'spec-coverage is the only reserved auditor id' would contradict an invariant this release does not touch. The pinned substring is now 'spec-coverage is the only auditor id that changes routing', and §4 states why that wording was chosen. §7 item 14 updated to match.

suggestion: Distinguish the two senses of 'reserved'. Keep the schema-level reservation (`regression` may not be authored) untouched and change the mandated substring to a routing-scoped phrasing such as `spec-coverage is the only auditor id tp routes on`, updating §2.1's wording and §7 item 14's pinned string to match; or keep the word 'reserved' but qualify it (`spec-coverage is the only auditor id reserved by the routing`) and state explicitly in §4 that the schema reservation of `regression` is unchanged.

finding: §4's first two requirements are each pinned as an exact substring and guarded by §7 item 14, but the third paragraph's two requirements are neither. (a) The prompt body-order lines in `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md` (line 400) and `skills/tp/SKILL.md` (line 309) must be rewritten to two named orders — the strings are given verbatim, so a substring guard is trivially writable, yet §7 has no item asserting them. (b) 'they must state instead that the value is any active role id from the corpus' is a semantic requirement with no pinned literal at all, so no deterministic pass/fail test exists and two engineers write different sentences. §4 itself observes that this same `prompts[].role` enum has been silently wrong since v0.25.0 — untested doc drift in exactly this place is a demonstrated, not hypothetical, failure mode.

resolved.evidence: §7 item 14 now guards the third paragraph too: it asserts REFERENCE.md and SKILL.md each carry the two §4 prompt-body orders verbatim and no longer state prompts[].role as an enum of the three built-in ids. Every §4 requirement is now guarded rather than only the first two.

suggestion: Pin a substring for the role-value statement the same way as the other two (for example `any active auditor role id from the corpus`), and extend §7 item 14 to assert the two rewritten body-order strings and that substring in both SKILL.md and REFERENCE.md.

finding: §6's round-3 arithmetic is stated 'per shared-arm prompt' but holds only for the `security` role. The two down/up terms are role-specific: (a) the -10 path lines exist only where the cap falls from 20 to 10, and per §2.5 only `security` was bounded by 20 — `maintainability-conventions` and every custom role already ran on MaintainabilityFileCap = 10 (§1: the maintainability arm is 'byte-for-byte what the default branch already computes'), so their cap does not move; (b) the +50 lines of §2.3 project conventions do not apply to `maintainability-conventions`, which is the one id that already received `## Project Context` (§1). The true per-prompt deltas are therefore roughly +45 lines for `security`, roughly +55 for a custom shared-arm role (conventions and Disposition added, cap unchanged), and roughly +5 for `maintainability-conventions` — not the single 'roughly 45 lines for a paths-only role' §6 states for all shared-arm prompts. The section that exists to be honest about cost understates the worst case (the custom role) by ~10 lines and overstates it by ~40 for the maintainability role.

resolved.evidence: Correct — the arithmetic was one role's numbers generalized across all of them, which is the same over-reach as the 'roughly unchanged' claim it replaced, inverted. §6 now carries a per-role table: security +~45 (the only role paying the −10, since every other already ran on the default branch's list at MaintainabilityFileCap), maintainability-conventions +~5 (the only role that already had the conventions block), any custom role +~55, spec-coverage ~0.

suggestion: Split §6's second paragraph by role category instead of asserting one per-prompt figure: state ~+45 for `security` (the only role whose cap falls 20→10), ~+55 for a custom/ejected shared-arm role (no cap change, gains both conventions and Disposition), and ~+5 for `maintainability-conventions` (already had `## Project Context`). Keep the closing 'claims to be free nowhere' summary and cite the +55 case as the worst one.

finding: §6's second paragraph states its arithmetic as holding "per shared-arm prompt" (three deltas up, one down, "roughly 45 lines for a paths-only role"), but the single downward delta — "up to 10 fewer affected-file path lines, since the cap falls from 20 to 10" — applies to exactly one role, `security`. Per §1 the `default` branch already computed `AuditFileSelection.Maintainability` for every other role, and §2.5 confirms that list's cap "stays 10": `maintainability-conventions` and every ejected/custom role were already bounded by 10, so their cap does not fall and they absorb the full upward delta (~+55 lines), not +45. Symmetrically, `maintainability-conventions` already received `## Project Context` (§2.3 removes a gate that already admitted it), so its §2.3 upward delta is zero and its true growth is ~+5 lines. The stated figure is therefore correct for one role out of the panel and wrong in both directions for the rest — and tp's own dogfooded 4-auditor corpus contains no `security` role at all, so the number describes zero of tp's own prompts. This understates the cost of the very panel-widening §6 exists to price honestly.

resolved.evidence: Same misattribution as the architect's cost-accounting-scope-drift finding, fixed together in §6's per-role table. This finding's identification of the §2.3 term as also role-specific (maintainability-conventions alone already received the conventions block) is what made the table four rows rather than two.

suggestion: Split the accounting by role class instead of asserting one per-prompt figure: (a) a role previously on the `security` arm: +50 conventions, +~5 Disposition, +header chars, −up to 10 path lines ⇒ ~+45; (b) a role previously on the `default` arm without conventions (every custom/ejected role): +50, +~5, +header, no cap reduction ⇒ ~+55; (c) `maintainability-conventions`, which already had both the 10-file cap and the conventions block: +~5 plus header chars. Then state the panel-level total honestly — in a corpus with no `security` role there is no downward delta anywhere.

finding: Item 4 says TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted loses only its `assert.Empty(t, sel.Security)` line and that 'the rest of the test stands', but the rest of that test also reads the renamed field: internal/engine/auditfiles_test.go:123-124 are `require.Len(t, sel.Maintainability, 1)` and `assert.Equal(t, "keep.go", sel.Maintainability[0].Path)`. Item 5, which enumerates the mechanical `sel.Maintainability`->`CodeFiles` renames, names only TestFilterFiles_Maintainability and TestFilterFiles_DropFirstBackfill. Since the section opens by declaring the inventory exhaustive against a search for `sel.Maintainability` and that 'the list itself is the contract', an implementer working the list literally leaves two references to a deleted field and the engine test package fails to compile.

resolved.evidence: Same as the two other §2.8 findings on this test, fixed together in item 4: both the deleted sel.Security line and the renamed sel.Maintainability lines are now stated, and item 5 no longer implies it covers them.

suggestion: Either add TestFilterFiles_DropsBinaryFixturesDeleted to item 5's rename list, or amend item 4 to read: the `sel.Security` assertion is deleted and the test's two remaining `sel.Maintainability` references are renamed to `sel.CodeFiles` like every other reference.

finding: Item 7 lists `TestAudit_FileFilterCap` under a heading that reads 'Existing tests this change invalidates', but that test stays green unmodified: its assertions are `assert.LessOrEqual(len(security affected_files), 20)` and `assert.LessOrEqual(len(maintainability affected_files), 10)` (internal/cli/integration_test.go:69-70), and a 10-entry list still satisfies both. So 'the expected count becomes 10 and the assertion is retargeted' is an instruction with no failing test behind it — an implementer who runs the suite and fixes what breaks leaves the only end-to-end cap test asserting a bound twice the real cap. Item 6 sets the precedent of stating a non-breaking entry explicitly ('does **not** break'); item 7 does not.

resolved.evidence: Correct and it changed the framing. TestAudit_FileFilterCap's assertions are LessOrEqual bounds, so a 10-entry list still satisfies a ≤20 assertion — the test does not break, it stops testing anything. §2.8 item 7 now says exactly that and tightens the bound to an exact 10, with the reason stated: a silently-loosened assertion is worse than a failing one.

suggestion: State in item 7 that the current `LessOrEqual(..., 20)` assertion still passes and must be tightened deliberately, and pin the retarget as an equality: `assert.Len(security affected_files, 10)`.

finding: §2.8 declares its inventory 'exhaustive against a search for every committed reference to' an enumerated token set, and adds 'The list itself is the contract'. The enumerated set covers only removed/renamed data (sel.Security, selectSecurity, HeadReader, securityHeadLineCap, headLines, containsSecuritySubstring, sel.Maintainability, selectMaintainability, MaintainabilityFileCap, roleSecurity, roleMaintainability, the two prompt literals and the two JSON role keys). It omits every identifier this spec renames or re-signatures elsewhere: `securitySubstrings` → `priorityPathSubstrings` (§2.4 item 2 — and §7 item 16 introduces a test asserting exactly that symbol's value), `routeChecklist` (§2.1 drops its `sel` argument and its sec/maint return values), and `generateRoleAuditPrompts` (§2.1 drops the `secItems`/`maintItems` parameters). A white-box test or helper that calls those symbols with the old arity but never mentions a listed token would break the build and is not in the inventory, so the stated exhaustiveness basis does not cover the compile-breaking half of the change.

resolved.evidence: §2.8's searched set is now a machine-readable ```search-literals fenced block that scripts/check-test-inventory.py reads, so the spec and the check cannot disagree about what was searched. The bare role ids are documented as deliberately absent with the measured reason (37 referencing tests, 27 unaffected), and the two tests reached only that way were hand-checked and shown green.

suggestion: Extend §2.8's enumerated search set with `securitySubstrings`, `routeChecklist`, and `generateRoleAuditPrompts` (the symbols renamed or re-signatured by §2.4 item 2 and §2.1), or narrow the exhaustiveness claim to 'exhaustive against references to removed or renamed data; signature changes to routeChecklist/generateRoleAuditPrompts surface at compile time and are fixed in place'.

finding: §6's second paragraph was rewritten this round from "Net prompt size for such a role is roughly unchanged" to explicit arithmetic, and in doing so it generalized single-role deltas across every shared-arm prompt — reproducing, inverted, the defect the round-3 finding raised against the old wording (a claim stated for every already-emitting role that holds for at most one). Two of its four terms are zero for roles other than `security`. (a) "§2.3 adds up to 50 lines of project conventions" adds nothing for `maintainability-conventions`, which already receives the block — that gate is the whole premise of §2.3 and §1 (internal/cli/audit_roles.go:220). (b) "up to 10 fewer affected-file path lines, since the cap falls from 20 to 10" is true only for the deleted per-role security list; every other non-spec-coverage role is already bounded by `MaintainabilityFileCap` = 10, which is exactly what unchanged §2.5 says when it states "The cap value stays 10". So the per-prompt delta is roughly +55 lines for a previously-default-branch role (new conventions block, no cap drop) and roughly +5 for `maintainability-conventions` — never the stated "roughly 45 lines", which holds only for a `security` role in a keyword-matching repository. A reader budgeting a multi-role panel from this paragraph gets every role wrong.

resolved.evidence: Same over-reach as the two other §6 findings, fixed together by the per-role table. The observation that the round-3 rewrite reproduced the round-3 defect inverted is recorded in §6's own text, so the next revision has the failure mode in front of it.

suggestion: Scope the arithmetic to the role it describes and state the other cases: keep the +50/+5/−10 ≈ +45 accounting for the `security` role in a repository where the keyword list already matched, then add that a role that took the `default` branch gains the conventions block with no offsetting cap drop (≈ +55, since §2.5 leaves its cap at 10) and that `maintainability-conventions` gains only the ~5-line Disposition block. Drop "per shared-arm prompt" from the framing sentence.

finding: Item 5 ('A file whose path does not match a keyword but whose first lines contain `validate` or `auth` is ranked as an ordinary file') does not say at which level the test lives, and after §2.4 item 3 removes `AuditFileInputs.HeadReader` there is no engine-level channel to supply file content at all — `SelectAuditFiles` takes paths only. Written as the natural sibling of item 4 (an engine test over `selectCodeFiles`, reusing `TestFilterFiles_Security`'s fixture per §2.8 item 3), the 'first lines contain validate' clause is not an input the API accepts, so the assertion cannot fail for any implementation and pins nothing. Only a CLI-level test with a real on-disk file whose head contains the keyword can detect an implementation that re-reads content from disk.

resolved.evidence: §7 item 5 now states the level explicitly: after §2.4 item 3 removes HeadReader there is no engine-level content channel, so the assertion is written at the CLI level where the file exists on disk, and the absence of a content channel is itself what it pins.

suggestion: State the level explicitly: a CLI-level audit over real files, one named with a non-matching path but containing `validate` in its first lines, asserting the emitted affected-files order is plain alphabetical. Alternatively drop the content fixture and state the assertion as 'AuditFileInputs exposes no content field', which is what the engine level can actually observe.

finding: Item 5 requires a test over 'a file whose path does not match a keyword but whose first lines contain `validate` or `auth`', but §2.4 item 3 removes `AuditFileInputs.HeadReader` — the only channel through which file content ever reached selection — and leaves AuditFileInputs holding Universe, DiffStats, Deleted, TaskFiles. Selection after the change is path-only and git-free, so an engine-level test (the level items 4 and 7 sit at, and the level TestFilterFiles_Security used via its HeadReader stub) has no way to give a file 'first lines' at all; the implementer must invent both where the content lives (working tree, or a committed file so it exists at HEAD) and at which level the test runs, and the engine-level reading degenerates into item 4's no-match case.

resolved.evidence: Same unconstructible fixture as the tester's untestable-after-seam-removal finding, fixed together in §7 item 5 by moving it to the CLI level and saying so.

suggestion: State the fixture: e.g. 'a CLI-level test over a git fixture whose committed file content contains `validate` while its path does not, asserting the file is not ranked ahead of an alphabetically earlier non-matching file' — or drop item 5 and note that §2.4 item 3's `unused`-linter argument plus item 16's exact-list assertion already pin the content half's removal.
